title: The state went looking for violent extremists in Minneapolis. So an agent offered to build them.
body: The Intercept's Matt Sledge got the court filing that shows how far the government went to surveil the left in Minneapolis. After federal agents killed Alex Pretti in January, ICE's Homeland Security Investigations opened two probes, "Operation Puppet Master" and "Project Whipple Shield," aimed at a supposed network of "violent opportunists and agitators." What the documents actually show is undercover agents sitting in on nonviolence trainings at churches, libraries, and schools, then filing reports on groups that kept saying, out loud, that they were peaceful.

The sharpest detail comes from a Sunrise Movement training at a public library. An undercover agent pulled an organizer aside, said he worked in construction, and offered to "build items that might assist other groups with more 'direct-action' protests." He added that "going to jail did not bother him." Sunrise preaches nonviolence in nearly every meeting it runs. So the agent was not documenting a threat. He was trying to build one. The defense attorney, Kevin Riach, said agents "actively participated in organizing and directing the groups they were surveilling."

ICE also subpoenaed years of Sunrise's bank records, back to 2023, along with those of unions like the CWA and SEIU. None of the 15 people eventually charged were Sunrise members. Dropsite and NOTUS covered the wider dragnet. Here's the tell. When the state has to send someone in to invent the crime, the movement it fears hasn't committed one.
